propositions: Compaction removed from close path holds a 13m53s store lock that starves concurrent agents; event logs now grow without bound until manual `rebar compact` is run.

A dedicated scheduled workflow (6-hourly) and an operation-linked fallback trigger (two O(1) checks on close, detached worker with stamped advisory lock) restore automatic compaction without reintroducing lock contention.

The sweep selects on two arms (backfill: no SNAPSHOT + foldable events; recurrence: foldable count > threshold) and counts only tickets where a new SNAPSHOT appears; this prevents selecting work the fold cannot perform and avoids per-ticket churn.

The git history walk for authorship ledger per ticket inside the write lock creates per-ticket O(history) overhead; when compacting many tickets it equals the prior per-event bug; the fix hoists the walk outside the lock and batches it to one per sweep.

Stores without CI and no cron must compact via operation-linked trigger; the sweep triggered by close-path checks must stand aside when the store lock is busy, and must re-yield between chunks so writes are not starved.

The advisory lock that gates the detached worker uses stamped ownership (pid + wall-clock ceiling) inherited from the drain lock, preventing storm and reclaiming stale locks; a tri-state config knob (async/always/off) makes the fold testable inline.
